dimensions: p=round(exp(U(log(50),log(500)))); n=p or max(50,floor(.8*p)); one frozen draw of dimensions per replicate.
selection: All prespecified settings and all repetitions are reported, regardless of model performance. No screening of evaluation settings.
fitting: No refitting, no changes to the current model or comparators.

sparse_linear.adaptation: Correlated Gaussian sparse linear family from the authors model-X vignette; retain rho=.25, amplitude=4.5, noise SD=1, and positive coefficients. Set k=10 instead of 60 for p as small as 50. Use the shared random n,p rule instead of the vignette fixed dimensions. X and y are not sample-standardized or centered by this generator.

friedman1.formula: 10 sin(pi X1 X2)+20(X3-.5)^2+10 X4+5 X5+N(0,1); independent Xj~Uniform(0,1)
friedman1.adaptation: Use sklearn.datasets.make_friedman1 directly, noise=1. Randomly permute columns after generating y; record the original five signal columns. No standardization before generating the response.

real: MNIST: official 60,000 training images flattened to 784 pixels. BASEHOCK: scikit-feature 1,993 by 4,862 text matrix. Sample n rows without replacement, sample p columns that vary in those rows, standardize selected columns. Plant six relevant columns and generate linear or square response, center/scale signal to SD1, add independent N(0,1), center y. Original labels are unused. These are real-X semi-simulations, not tests on original labels.
overlap: Both are standard benchmark families; response families can overlap model development. New random draws and the two new real predictor pools are used. No claim that all mechanisms were unseen.
